title: Concerns raised over delayed Colombo Port crane removal tender - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 27 (Daily Mirror) - The tender to remove four old gantry cranes from the Colombo Port’s Jaya Container Terminal has been delayed for the third time, causing concerns among several bidders.

The tender, valued at over Rs. 200 million, was first scheduled to close on July 16, then postponed to July 28, and has now been extended until August 11.

Several bidders have reportedly requested President Anura Kumara Dissanayake to review the tender process, claiming that reducing the number of bidders from 11 to two could reduce competition and affect government revenue.

Port sector officials said several experienced companies that had submitted bids were removed from the final selection. They also claimed that companies involved in previous crane removal projects at the Colombo Port were among those excluded.

Some bidders questioned the decision to have the same tender committee consider appeals submitted by rejected applicants, saying an independent committee should review such appeals.

They also raised concerns that the process could favour a particular bidder, though no evidence has been presented to support the claim.

Sri Lanka Ports Authority Chairman Parakrama Dissanayake said the tender process was still ongoing and approvals were being obtained. He said the process was being handled by two committees and it was not appropriate to comment further at this stage.

The four gantry cranes, installed in the 1980s, have become outdated and the SLPA has decided to remove them as part of efforts to modernise port operations.

title: President discusses issues in developing cricket in Sri Lanka - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 27 (Daily Mirror) - President Anura Kumara Dissanayake held a meeting with the Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC)

Transformation Committee where he discussed the issues and challenges faced in developing cricket in Sri Lanka.

The meeting was held at the Presidential Secretariat this afternoon, the President’s Media Division (PMD) said.

The President also considered the support and contribution that could be provided by the Government towards the continued progress and advancement of cricket in the country.

Minister of Youth Affairs and Sports Sunil Kumara Gamage, Chief of Staff to the President Prabath Chandrakeerthi, Chairman of the Sri Lanka Cricket Transformation Committee Eran Wickramaratne and committee members Roshan Mahanama, Avanthi Colombage, Upul Kumarapperuma, Thushira Radella, Sidath Wettimuny and Dinal Philip also participated in the meeting.

title: Kavadi dances allowed at Devinuwara Perahera despite earlier police concerns - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 27 (Daily Mirror) - Public Security Minister Ananda Wijepala has granted permission for all 45 Kavadi dance troupes that participated in last year’s procession to take part in this year’s Devinuwara Esala Perahera.

The decision comes after police had earlier recommended removing the traditional Kavadi dance performances from the procession due to security concerns.

The decision was finalized during a special discussion held this afternoon (27) at the Matara District Secretariat.

The meeting was chaired by Minister Ananda Wijepala and attended by Public Security Ministry Secretary Ravi Seneviratne, Inspector General of Police (IGP) Priyantha Weerasooriya, Matara District Secretary Chandana Thilakarathne and other officials.

Meanwhile, additional personnel from the Sri Lanka Police and the Police Special Task Force (STF) will be deployed to strengthen security for the procession, which is scheduled to be held tomorrow (28).

title: Sri Lanka, India review progress of key development projects - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 27 (Daily Mirror) - Minister of Labour and Deputy Minister of Finance and Planning Dr. Anil Jayantha Fernando today held discussions with Indian High Commissioner to Sri Lanka Santosh Jha to review the progress of development projects being implemented with financial assistance from the Government of India.

The meeting, held at the Presidential Secretariat, focused on challenges affecting the implementation of Indian-funded infrastructure projects and measures required to address them. Discussions also covered the renewal of agreements needed to ensure the continuation of the projects.

The projects under review are being implemented through several ministries, including Transport, Highways and Urban Development, Ports and Civil Aviation, Plantations and Community Infrastructure, Housing Construction and Water Supply, Fisheries, Science and Technology, and Justice and National Integration.

The discussions also reviewed projects financed through the US$450 million loan and grant assistance provided by the Government of India for disaster recovery and reconstruction.

Participants further discussed establishing a dedicated unit within the Presidential Secretariat to oversee and monitor the implementation of India-funded development projects.

The meeting was attended by Chief of Staff to the President Prabath Chandrakeerthi, Finance Ministry Secretary Dr. Harshana Suriyapperuma, Fisheries Ministry Secretary Dr. Kolitha Kamal Jinadasa, officials from the Presidential Secretariat and the Ministry of Finance, as well as Deputy High Commissioner of India Maitrey Kulkarni and other officials from the Indian High Commission.

title: US, Sri Lanka launch CARAT 2026 maritime exercise - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 27 (Daily Mirror) - The United States and Sri Lanka have launched the sixth edition of the Cooperation Afloat Readiness and Training (CARAT) exercise, a bilateral maritime program aimed at strengthening cooperation in maritime security, humanitarian assistance, disaster response, and regional readiness.

Hosted by the Sri Lanka Navy in Trincomalee and Colombo from July 27 to 31, CARAT Sri Lanka 2026 brings together personnel from the U.S. Navy, U.S. Coast Guard, Sri Lanka Navy, and Sri Lanka Air Force for a week of shore- and sea-based training.

The exercise includes classroom sessions and practical training in maritime domain awareness, tactical medicine, explosive ordnance disposal, and visit, board, search and seizure (VBSS) operations before participants conduct joint activities at sea.

A U.S. Navy P-8A Poseidon maritime patrol and reconnaissance aircraft will support maritime surveillance training, while a U.S. Coast Guard Maritime Engagement Team will conduct training aboard SLNS Gajabahu (P626), the former U.S. Coast Guard Cutter Douglas Munro transferred to Sri Lanka by the United States. The team will also employ a U.S.-provided rigid-hull inflatable boat during maritime operations.

U.S. Embassy Senior Defense Official and Defense Attaché to Sri Lanka, Lt. Col. Matthew House, said the exercise reflects the United States' enduring commitment to its security partnership with Sri Lanka.

"When our sailors train side-by-side, they build the trust, interoperability, and professional relationships that allow us to respond more effectively together when it matters most," he said.

In addition to operational training, the exercise includes community service projects, sporting events, and cultural exchanges designed to strengthen ties between service members.

The annual CARAT exercise, held in Sri Lanka since 2017, is aimed at enhancing interoperability between the two countries' armed forces and improving their ability to respond jointly to maritime security challenges, search and rescue missions, natural disasters, and other regional threats in the Indian Ocean.

title: Rs. 200,000 paid to shoot Dehiwala Cemetery guard; Gunman arrested - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 27 (Daily Mirror) - Police have arrested the alleged gunman involved in the shooting of a security guard at the Nisala Sewana public cemetery in Dehiwala-Mount Lavinia, Deputy Inspector General (DIG) of Police for the Colombo District, Nishantha de Zoysa, said today (27).

The shooting took place on July 19 when two men arrived on a scooter-type motorcycle and opened fire on the cemetery guard before fleeing the scene. The attackers allegedly used a 9mm firearm.

The victim, a 56-year-old resident of the Dehiwala Fishermen's Housing area, sustained gunshot injuries to his left arm and chest and was admitted to the Kalubowila Teaching Hospital for treatment.

Police had earlier arrested the motorcycle rider in the Delkanda area on July 26. During the arrest, officers recovered 7 grams and 200 milligrams of crystal methamphetamine ("Ice") from the 25-year-old suspect.

According to police, investigations revealed that the shooting had been carried out on the instructions of an organized criminal believed to be hiding overseas. The suspects had allegedly been promised Rs. 200,000 to carry out the attack.

Police also recovered Rs. 55,000, believed to be part of the payment for the shooting, along with three mobile phones allegedly used by the suspect during the operation.

Investigations into the incident are continuing.

title: Horana tuition centre owner arrested with crystal meth - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 27 (Daily Mirror) - The owner of a private tuition centre in Horana has been arrested for allegedly possessing the narcotic drug known as "Ice" (crystal methamphetamine), police said.

The suspect, a 44-year-old resident of the Narthanagala area in Horana, was taken into custody during a police raid at his residence.

Police said they recovered 15g 250mg of crystal methamphetamine from the suspect's possession. Officers also seized a mobile phone, a SIM card believed to have been used for drug trafficking activities, and an electronic weighing scale.

According to investigators, the suspect attempted to flee when police arrived at his residence but was apprehended after a brief pursuit.

Preliminary investigations have revealed that the suspect is the son of a well-known businessman in the Horana area. Police further said that he has previously faced several drug-related charges.

Police are also probing whether the suspect had links to organized drug trafficking networks, operated a wider drug distribution operation, and whether narcotics were supplied to students attending his tuition classes.
